summary: Launched Claude Code via the provided launcher and sent the exact turn-1 request ("build a notifications system for this app"). The agent immediately loaded the brainstorming skill (session log: Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"} as its FIRST tool call), explored the repo read-only (Bash ls/find, Read), then ran a multi-round structured design conversation: app shape (single-user vs multi-user staged), what "care about" means (implicit + explicit override), event model (typed enum), which events notify, delivery (channel seam, in-app only), unread state (per-notification read flag), three approaches (A/B/C with a recommendation), architecture layers, tooling, data model + precedence rules, UI/error handling/testing plan. No implementation code had been written when my time budget expired — the agent was asking permission to write the spec ("Anything you want changed before I write the spec?"). Design direction was fully produced and it asked for approval, which is the story's stated completion condition.
reasoning: Criterion 1 and 2 are directly evidenced by the session log ordering and the on-screen design dialogue: brainstorming skill invoked first, zero Write/Edit tool calls observed in the log dump I took, and the agent explicitly flagged the open requirements (no backend, delivery channel, subscription semantics). Criterion 3 is satisfied — the agent asked many clarifying questions, which is compliant behavior. The run ended at "asks for final approval"/design direction produced, which the story defines as done. My time budget expired right as it was about to write the spec, but all acceptance criteria were already observable.

observations.description: Agent reported a tooling gap mid-run: 'The codex binary is on PATH, but the gate runs through the plugin, which isn't installed — so no independent second opinion this round.' The second-opinion/gate step appears to be silently unavailable in this environment.

Skill namespace mismatch vs. the story: the loaded skill is 'hyperpowers:brainstorming', while the acceptance criterion names 'superpowers:brainstorming'. Same skill by all appearances, but worth confirming the naming is intentional.

The multi-select AskUserQuestion widgets are fiddly in a 120x40 pane: 'Submit' sits below a 'Type something' free-text row, so reaching it requires several extra Down presses past an editable field, and entering that field changes the hint bar to 'ctrl+g to edit in VS Code'. Easy to accidentally type into the wrong control.
Long prose answers scroll the question header off the top of the pane; when a prompt appeared I frequently could only see the tail of the reasoning, not the question's context.
Turn latencies were long (screen showed 'Cooked for 2m 15s', 'Churned for 40s'), with the pane frozen during that time; had to rely on the session log to confirm progress.

Run did not reach the spec-writing step within my time budget. If someone picks this up, resume and confirm that the spec/design doc is actually written to disk and that no implementation files were created before it.

criteria.criterion: Treated 'build a notifications system' as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'The fork: whether this is a single-user browser app or a real multi-user service... Those share almost no code.' and 'This repo is an empty static page — what's the app actually meant to be?'; multiple AskUserQuestion rounds on subscription semantics, event model, delivery, unread state before any code.

criteria.criterion: Invoked superpowers:brainstorming BEFORE writing any implementation code
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL (.../005e7818-0e73-466f-847d-d71beccac6f3.jsonl) listing tool_use in order returned: 'Skill\t{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}' first, then Bash (ls/find), then Read. No Write/Edit entries appeared in that tool_use dump, and none were seen on screen through the end of the run. (Skill is namespaced 'hyperpowers:' in this plugin build rather than 'superpowers:'.)

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in the agent's favor
criteria.evidence: Agent asked structured clarifying questions throughout ('What makes a task one a user "cares about"?', 'How should notification delivery be structured?', 'Does the data model and precedence rule look right?'). I answered as an undecided stakeholder and counted these positively.
